name: hold-and-release
description: Renamed from "cradle-and-release" (epic context, Code Map): this placeholder table has no pocket geometry beside either flipper, so a golden claiming a multi-second cradle would freeze roll-off as the cradle reference. This golden presses the left flipper for 600 ticks (0.6 s, well inside the ~1 s stable window) starting at tick 8650, just after the orbit-routed ball reaches the left bat band at tick 8639 [CORRECTED 2026-09-03, code review: this read "just before ... at tick 8639" against a recorded press of 8650, i.e. eleven ticks after, not before], then releases; the ball is still in play at durationTicks, as this golden's own notes state. Story 2.1c retimed the press from 9700/10300 to 8650/9250 and durationTicks from 10500 to 9600 when the orbit routing moved the ball's arrival -- at the old timings the hold fell entirely after the ball had already drained. Pins the coil hardware rule (energise/de-energise) against a real ball, not a literal rest-on-bat cradle.

flipperTipGapMm.source: authored: derived arithmetic, not a second invented figure -- the gap between the right bat's tip (col_flipper_r.bboxMm.min.x = 277.525 mm) and the left bat's tip (col_flipper_l.bboxMm.max.x = 236.875 mm) at end-of-stroke, both a direct consequence of DW-78's reconciliation (each box moved outward by baseRadius = 12.5 mm around its own unchanged pivot). No planning artifact states a tip gap the sourced 9.5-12.7 mm figure (digests/geometry-r1-1.md:91,204, low confidence) is narrower than the 26.99 mm reference ball and therefore unusable as authored truth (Code Map, "Read-only evidence")

dampingScale.source: authored: upstream reads this from Settings::GetPlayer_PlumbDamping(), a user setting with no value in any of the seven authorized vpinball/vpinball files -- 1.0 (identity) is the most defensible 'no adjustment' choice against the transcribed dampingCoef0/dampingCoef1 ratio coefficients; measured during this story's implementation (see spec Verification section) to leave a single ordinary nudge's peak swing (~1.05 deg) well clear of thresholdDeg while still permitting a rapid nudge burst to cross it and decay away within a few seconds. Story 1.9's feel ritual ratifies it

thresholdDeg.source: authored: upstream reads this from Settings::GetPlayer_PlumbThresholdAngle(), a user setting with no value in any of the seven authorized vpinball/vpinball files -- measured during this story's implementation (see spec Verification section) so that ONE ordinary nudge_* rising edge (peak swing ~1.05 deg, measured) never crosses it, while a rapid burst of nudges (a deliberate, violent 'slam'-style burst) does. Story 1.9's feel ritual ratifies it against the Reference machine

notes: stateHash() hashes the whole game tree, which includes machine.deviceSlots -- this golden therefore freezes the LOOP-WRITTEN value of deviceSlots (sim/loop/index.ts:326-329, the live AD-7 violation tracked as DW-70) as part of its reference hash. If Story 2.5's fix is faithful the values will be identical and nothing breaks; if this golden ever breaks on deviceSlots alone, check DW-70 before assuming the physics changed. Story 2.1b (2026-09-01): header.tableHash/assetHash refreshed (bd_lock's new deviceSlots entry -- see the sibling goldens' own notes). Rework iteration 2 (2026-09-01), correcting this note: the sentence that used to stand here -- blaming "Blender's alphabetical bpy.data.objects ordering" reshuffling existing nodes' own array positions, with an "order-sensitive broadphase" -- was investigated and found FALSE, twice: the collision document is alphabetically sorted throughout, so the ~28 new names interleave among the existing ones rather than reshuffling their relative order, and a document rebuilt with the rework's own wall-height and deflector changes reverted reproduces the two affected goldens bit-identically, ruling out node reordering as the mechanism. The TRUE cause of the two affected goldens' own trajectory divergence was not identified by either the implement pass or this rework; DW-53's wall-height change (col_wall_left/_top/_right/_lane now reaching the glass) and DW-58's col_lane_deflector removal were both tested and ruled out individually (each reproduces the divergence bit-identically when reverted alone). State plainly rather than guess further: the trajectory changed because the shot map's own regeneration changed the collision document in some way this investigation did not isolate -- not because of the specific mechanism previously claimed here. expectedHash/expectedGameStateHash were refreshed to the current, correctly-computed values for the UNCHANGED (byte-identical) recorded transitions/coilPrologue/durationTicks. FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED: re-verifying this golden's own scenario claim against the refreshed run found the claim no longer holds within the recorded durationTicks -- this story's own Boundaries & Constraints treats a durationTicks (or scenario-assertion) change as a Block If, so this implementation pass halted short of that change and left the affected test(s) red rather than silently widening the window or the threshold. See this implementation pass's own final report for the measured detail. Rework iteration 2 (2026-09-01): re-verified against the geometry this pass actually shipped (the flat-topped-body bevels and the DRAGON-bank backstop wall) -- none of which lie anywhere near this golden's own trajectory (the ball and both flippers stay well below y = 420, confirmed by inspection). The scenario claim still does not hold: the raised bat's own measured deflection (0.027 mm, against the golden's own pinned >5 mm threshold) is essentially unchanged from the implement pass's own measurement. Not re-investigated further this pass -- the divergence is nowhere near the shot map this story owns, and finding its real cause (something in the lower-table geometry or the flipper/ball contact resolution, not the shot map) is outside what task list items 1-3 scope to. Left red for the lead, per this story's own Boundaries & Constraints (a scenario-assertion or durationTicks change is a Block If this story may not make unilaterally). Rework iteration 3 (2026-09-02, DW-121 / answer A/C): re-recorded under the same narrow exception, for the same reason as the sibling roll-and-drain golden -- the OLD press/release window (tick 7300/8100) was tuned to the pre-shot-map table's much shorter plunge-to-flipper travel time and no longer brackets when the ball genuinely arrives. Traced against the real runReplay() harness with this golden's own unchanged coilPrologue (serve + full autolaunch at tick 5021): the ball crosses the top (same trajectory as roll-and-drain's own, confirmed identical up to the press tick, since no flipper input differs before then) and is squarely in the flipper-reachable band by tick ~9700-10300. New press tick 9700, release tick 10300 (600-tick hold, the same order of magnitude as the original 800-tick hold), durationTicks widened to 10500. Re-verified against a paired no-flipper control run of this identical golden with transitions removed (the same idiom the covering test already uses): the flipper reaches end-of-stroke (90 deg) within 60 ticks of the press and is still held at the release tick, and the raised bat measurably deflects the ball -- maximum divergence from the control run 116.6 mm (first exceeding 1 mm at tick 10060, 360 ticks after the press), well above the covering test's own 5 mm threshold and roughly 2.4x the previous recording's own measured 48.3 mm. The ball is still in play at the new durationTicks (this golden pins contact, not a subsequent drain -- roll-and-drain's own re-record already covers the natural-drain claim). DW-121 is independently pinned by test/drain-switch-coverage.test.ts (see the sibling roll-and-drain golden's own note for detail). Story 2.1c (2026-09-03), the ORBIT: header.assetHash refreshed and the trajectory RE-RECORDED, with the press retimed to the new path. The autolaunched ball now takes the orbit's own longer route (top connector re-joined, left return rail, inlane feed), reaching the left bat band at tick 8639 and draining at 9293 with no input, so the old 9700/10300 press fell entirely AFTER the ball had gone -- the hold held nothing. Press 8650, release 9250 puts the whole 600-tick hold inside the window the control run still has a ball in, and durationTicks 10500 -> 9600 keeps the pressed ball in play at the end (as this golden's own description claims) while the control has drained, so the parity hash stays body-sensitive. Measured divergence against the no-flipper control: 103.8 mm, against this golden's own > 5 mm floor. Code review pass 2 rework (2026-09-03): header.assetHash refreshed (two geometry fixes elsewhere on the table -- a DRAGON-bank/leg-width re-solve, and a col_loop_top north-face ridge fixing a genuine DW-119 stranding on that connector's own flat top). expectedHash also moved (d0e7bccc -> f6eacd) -- expectedGameStateHash did NOT (9f72ccc unchanged), so this golden's own game-relevant state (switches, the flipper's own end-of-stroke angle, scores) is byte-identical; only the exact quantised ball position at the final tick shifted by a small amount, the same shared-serve/autolaunch-prologue ripple the other four goldens' own re-records this pass describe. Re-verified against the real pipeline before recording: this golden's own scenario check (contact, hold, deflection vs. the no-flipper control) passes unchanged with the same shape of evidence.
